subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Linear Motors: Motion in a Straight Line
description: A quick win: understand Linear Motors: Motion in a Straight Line.

hook.text: Unroll a rotary motor flat and it pushes in a straight line. That's a linear motor.

buildup.text: A traveling magnetic wave in the stator drags the rotor plate along without contact.

discovery.text: No gears, no belts, no rotary-to-linear conversion — direct thrust.

twist.text: Maglev trains use linear motors — they levitate and propel with no physical contact.

climax.text: Theme park launches, factory conveyors, and airport shuttles all use linear motors.

punchline.text: Unroll the motor and it pushes instead of spins — direct linear thrust.

quiz.question: What is a linear motor?
options: A motor with its stator and rotor unrolled flat for straight-line force
A motor that only runs at constant speed
A motor that converts linear motion into rotary motion
